answer: A verifiable delay rule gives an identity weight only after one operator completes a timed sequence that cannot be parallelized: the operator walks a marble 100 meters along a jetty, sets it on a scale, then waits while a pulse generator emits exactly 10,000 pulses at 10 per second before the reading is accepted. A reading taken before the pulse count finishes, a marble under 500 grams, or the same crossing time for two identities voids both attempts, so 100 fakes need 100 separate marbles, crossings, and 1,000-second waits.
